title: Principal Applied Research Engineer
description:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

The opportunity

At Synthesia we really care about video generation, especially about human centric avatar video generation. This led us to release models such as EXPRESS-Video, and soon our latest video model - these are the best avatar video models in the world, and we are committed to continuing and double down our efforts in leading that area. Our goal is to get to human centric video models that can generate arbitrary long videos at high resolution with arbitrary actions and events. That means continuously training large generative video models from scratch with the proprietary data pipelines and compute infrastructure to support it at scale. We are looking for a technical leader who owns the full stack end-to-end, someone who bridges pre-training and post-training, sets long-term direction alongside research leadership, and is personally present at the hardest parts of the work. If building foundation model capability from the ground up at a company genuinely committed to leading the field sounds like the right next challenge, this role was written for you.

About the role

Synthesia's video generation capability is core to everything we ship. It involves roughly 15 people working daily across pre-training and post-training stages, and the complexity of coordinating across those stages, at the scale of compute and data we now operate, requires a different kind of technical leadership.

We're looking for a Principal Research Engineer (L7) to own the full technical stack for offline video generation. This is a senior individual contributor position with outsized scope and influence. You'll partner directly with research leadership and team leads to define long-term strategy, resolve the hardest cross-cutting technical problems, and raise the bar for how quickly research reaches product.

The person we're looking for has trained large generative models from scratch, not supervised it from a distance, but done it, debugged it, and shipped it. More than that, they're driven by a genuine ambition to push what's possible in video generation, and they care deeply about seeing that work land in product and reach users.

What you'll do

  • Own the end-to-end technical direction for offline video generation, spanning pre-training and post-training, resolving the artificial boundary between those two stages in service of shipping better models faster.

  • Partner with research leadership and team leads to define a unified long-term roadmap, broken into achievable objectives, and drive execution against it.

  • Identify the most critical technical gaps across the video generation pipeline and jump in to unblock them, whether that means architectural decisions, training stability, post-training alignment, or cross-team coordination.

  • Increase the velocity at which research ships to product: accelerate problem-solving, improve research-to-production handoffs, and increase visibility of research output in partnership with PMs.

  • Coach and elevate more junior researchers and engineers toward senior technical thinking and execution.

  • Help shape team structure and refine processes to enable high-velocity, cohesive execution across research.

You'll thrive in this role if you have

  • A proven track record training large-scale video generation models from scratch, across multiple nodes, at the scale of millions of hours of data.

  • Deep experience with post-training techniques at scale: RLHF, GRPO, DPO, and the judgment to know when and how to apply them.

  • A proven track record data quality and you are not reluctant to question it.

  • The ability to think strategically about multi-year research direction and execute hands-on at the frontier of what the team is building.

  • Strong cross-functional influence: you shape how teams work together without needing positional authority to do it.

  • A leadership style grounded in technical involvement. You lead by example, inspire through craft, and communicate with clarity.

  • Genuine hunger to unlock new capabilities and an obsession with shipping. You're not satisfied by research that stays in a notebook. You want it in the hands of users.

Particularly relevant experience

  • Having owned a major model generation or capability jump end-to-end, from training runs through to product deployment.

  • Working across both pre-training and post-training stages on the same model family, with direct accountability for the outcomes of both.

  • Experience operating at scale: large distributed training runs, significant compute budgets, and multi-million hour data pipelines.

  • Applying alignment and fine-tuning techniques in a video or multimodal context, not just text.

  • Experience with human feedback pipelines applied to generative video or audio.

  • Leading or significantly influencing the technical direction of a research team while remaining hands-on.

Dealbreakers

We will not be a good fit if you prefer to lead without staying technically involved, or if clear and direct communication across research and product isn't one of your strengths. This role requires presence at the frontier of the work, not above it. And if shipping doesn't excite you as much as the research itself, this probably isn't the right role.

Oak Wood School is looking to appoint highly organised, efficient and compassionate Welfare Administrator to support the Welfare Officer in running of the school medical room and supplies, maintain accurate medical records and support administration of the first aid.

The ideal candidate will need to be well organised, flexible and have proven experience of working in a busy administrative role. Oak Wood School was judged as a ‘Good’ school by Ofsted (May 2022) and is a truly inclusive, mixed, multi-ethnic 11-18 school that embraces all aspects of comprehensive education. A career at Oak Wood School is your chance to be part of a remarkable team that are working to ensure our students are prepared to be the well- rounded leaders of tomorrow.

Contract type: Permanent 

Start date: 1st January 2027

FTE: 1FTE

Location: The King Alfred School, TA9 3EE


The King Alfred's School, is seeking an enthusiastic, organised and inspiring Teacher of Music and Tutor to join our vibrant school community.


About the role

We believe that students should have access to the highest calibre of performing arts whilst experiencing a wide range of creative opportunities to broaden their understanding of the world, through the curriculum and beyond. You will work closely with others in the department to help grow the confidence of students through enrichment opportunities. In this role, you won’t just deliver a curriculum—you will shape futures, foster inclusive learning environments, and provide the vital pastoral support that helps young people thrive.

What you’ll do:

  • Create clear learning objectives and lesson structures that maintain a high pace, motivation, and challenge for all students

  • Maintain high standards of student behavior through positive relationships and well-focused teaching 
  • Mark and monitor students’ work and set targets for progress in line with the learning and teaching and assessment policies.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for a tutor group, providing academic monitoring, guidance and pastoral welfare while liaising with parents and external agencies.

About you

  • You are a qualified teacher possessing QTS with proven experience teaching across a range of ages and abilities. 
  • You demonstrate a clear passion for Music and a deep commitment to sharing this enthusiasm with young people.
  • You have a detailed working knowledge of the National Curriculum requirements and the pedagogical skills to translate them into impactful, deep learning experiences.

At The King Alfred School, we are proud to provide a first-class education in a safe, happy and caring environment where every child is supported to reach their full potential. Our Somerset location offers strong transport links across Somerset and North Somerset, connecting our vibrant school community.

We foster an ethos built on kindness, ambition, resilience and mutual respect, which is reflected in our broad and balanced curriculum and high standards of student conduct. We feature a thriving Sixth Form centre, a dedicated Community Council and student leadership team, the student-led Jill Dando News Centre, and a strong track record of active involvement in our local community.

We can offer you:

  • Happy, engaging students who thrive on inspirational leadership
  • A supportive trust and school community
  • Strong collaboration across the trust family of schools and access to a centralised team of specialists across all areas of school operations
  • A commitment to high‑quality CPD, with dedicated time and budget for your development
  • A values‑driven ethos where diversity, equity and inclusion are lived every day
  • Recognition of continuous service (modification order) to protect employment rights and entitlements
  • Access to Health Shield, a fully funded healthcare scheme
  • Teachers’ Pension Scheme with generous employer contributions and death‑in‑service cover
  • Occupational sick pay to support you during illness or unexpected emergencies
  • Family‑friendly leave packages to help maintain a healthy work–life balance


In order to apply for this role please complete an application form by 9am, Tuesday 20th October. Interviews are expected to take place on Friday 23rd October. Please let us know if you require any adjustments as part of the process. 


Please know that depending on the number of applications received we may decide to close the advert early. If you do not hear from us by a week after the closing date then please assume that you have not been shortlisted for an interview. We wish you all the best in your future and ask that you join our E-Teach Talent Pool so as to keep up to date with all of our latest current opportunities.

Pathway Trust is committed to equal opportunities and encourages applicants from all backgrounds and communities, as we recognise the importance and benefit this has for our pupils.

Location: Newham Community Learning Trust Central Office, Pretoria Rd, London E16 4NP (Eastlea Community School)

Closing Date: 23rd October 2026

***We are seeking to appoint an experienced Chief Financial Officer to lead the Trust’s financial strategy, sustainability and governance, and to provide strategic financial leadership to the CEO, Executive Team and Trustees***

Newham Community Learning is a Multi-Academy Trust serving children and young people in East London. We believe every young person deserves an excellent education, whatever their background. Our commitment to equality and social justice shapes how we lead, how we spend, and how we hold ourselves to account.

The Role

  • A supportive, values-led culture in the heart of London.

How to Apply

Location: Unity Schools Partnership Trust Office (Working with our schools across East Anglia and north-east London)

Contract: 37 hours per week, 52 weeks per year, permanent (hybrid with regular attendance at Trust offices and travel to schools as required)

Salary: Grade 8 SP 40-45, (£59,474 to £66,076 per annum).

Job Start: As soon as possible

Annual leave: 24 days holiday rising to 29 days holiday after 5 years’ service plus bank holidays

Pension: Local Government Pension Scheme

Play a key strategic role in improving attendance and transforming outcomes for pupils

Unity Schools Partnership (40 primary, secondary and special schools across East Anglia and north‑east London) is seeking an exceptional Trust Attendance Lead to drive our Trust-wide attendance strategy and support schools to secure lasting improvements in pupil attendance, engagement and achievement.

Why this role matters

Attendance is one of the most significant factors influencing educational outcomes, safeguarding and life chances. This is a strategic leadership role at the centre of our school improvement work. Working alongside Trust and school leaders, you will shape and deliver our attendance strategy, use of data and evidence to identify priorities and trends, quality assure practice across schools and provide expert support and challenge to leaders. You will help build leadership capacity, strengthen systems and ensure that effective attendance practice is embedded consistently across our schools, resulting in positive outcomes for pupils and families.

What we’re looking for

You’ll bring:

  • Experience of working with school and Trust leaders, to deliver improvement across multiple settings;
  • The ability to strategically analyse complex information and turn data into meaningful action and impact;
  • Sound judgement, resilience and the ability to build effective relationships while maintaining professional challenge;
  • A strong understanding of attendance, safeguarding, inclusion, SEND and the wider factors affecting pupil engagement;
  • Professional judgement, discretion and a real commitment to confidentiality and safeguarding;
  • A commitment to inclusion, equality and our values of integrity, inclusion and kindness;
  • Skill in building and maintaining positive relationships with a variety of stakeholders.


Closing Date: 9.00 am, Monday 2nd November 2026

Interviews: Wednesday 11th November 2026

For an informal discussion, contact Lisa Taylor, Trust Secretary via ltaylor@unitysp.co.uk or by calling 01440 333400

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applications from under-represented groups as well as colleagues from majority groups who share our values. Flexible working options, including part-time and job-share will be considered.

Unity Schools Partnership is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. An enhanced DBS check will be required.

We would like to hear if you have:

  • QTS (or equivalent) and a relevant undergraduate degree
  • At least three years' teaching experience
  • At least two years in a management role.
  • Experience of teaching Mathematics to A-Level
  • Clear evidence of having raised standards of achievement at all levels

  • Experience in observing and evaluating teacher quality, and providing feedback

  • Evidence of being an excellent teacher

You will benefit from the support of a dedicated Deputy Principal, the wider SLT and the specialist resources of The Collegiate Trust central team.

TQA is a great place for professional growth. Colleagues benefit from regular, weekly CPD, 1:1 instructional coaching, a bespoke Professional Development Journal and access to NPQ and Masters programmes. Our motto, “Learning Changes Lives”, applies as much to staff as it does to students, and it gives an indication of the significance we place on nurturing talent and leadership at every level.

description:
Attendance & Family Liaison Officer

Start date: December 2026

Salary: Full Time Equivalent £28,886 / Actual £24,925

Hours: 37.5 per week, 8am - 4pm Monday to Friday with flexibility required during exam periods

Contract type: Permanent

We are seeking to appoint an enthusiastic and committed person to join us as our Attendance & Family Liaison Officer Assistant. This rewarding role focuses on supporting students who are severely absent from education, helping them to overcome barriers and successfully re-engage with learning. Working as part of a dedicated and supportive team, you will play a key role in promoting the attendance, welfare, and educational outcomes of some of our most vulnerable students.

You will work closely with families, school staff, external agencies, and the SEND team to identify the challenges affecting attendance and develop effective strategies to address them. The ideal candidate will have:

title: Regional Director and Executive Principal
description:
Who we’re looking for

Star Academies is looking for a highly experienced secondary school leader with the ability and authority to lead improvements in standards across our primary and secondary schools in Greater Manchester and Preston.

You will oversee a portfolio of schools across Greater Manchester and Preston, currently five secondary and two primary schools.

Star is a mixed multi academy trust made up of Muslim, Christian and non-faith schools. The person appointed must be comfortable with and have an understanding of working in faith and non-faith settings.

You will be credible and with a proven background in sustainable school improvement, particularly with secondary schools. You will be able to identify priorities, put in place interventions to secure gains in pupil outcomes, and work with our school Principals to make it happen, and empower them to lead and build capacity.

You will have a track record of successful school leadership with a clear understanding of how to deliver the highest possible standards across schools with differing contexts and improvement journeys. You will also be able to line manage school Principals, holding them to account for standards and outcomes, and where necessary coach and guide them to improve their own practice and that of others.

The position requires an individual who can work both strategically and operationally, consistently modelling best practice in leadership and pedagogy on a daily basis, and does not adopt a ‘one size fits all’ approach.


You will have:

  • Credibility as an experienced and successful Principal with a demonstrable track record of success, in a secondary phase setting. Experience in the primary phase is desirable but not essential.
  • The ability to lead, manage, develop and inspire school leaders to secure standards and outcomes consistent with the aspiration of top 5% performance nationally.
  • The ability to support Principals and school leaders to manage change rapidly and sustainably.
  • A proven record in school improvement, school-to-school support strategies, and how to implement them effectively.
  • Strong strategic and operational planning skills.
  • An understanding of the benefits and dynamics of wider partnerships in localities and regions
  • Full commitment to our mission, vision and values.
  • Strong personal skills to flex in different contexts and situations to bring out the best in others.

title: AI Experience Engineer (Conversational AI)
description:
Headquarters: Canada (Remote)

 About the Role:

An AI Experience Engineer owns the full lifecycle of the journeys our customers have with Upgrade's AI agent on chat, voice and email: creation, optimization, edge case handling and containment growth. They build journeys in Sierra's no-code tooling, partner with Upgrade's product groups to bring their servicing flows to the agent, and are accountable for whether the agent resolves the customer's issue safely, accurately and without a human.

 We are hiring an AI Experience Engineer to own Upgrade's customer-facing AI agent. You will sit between engineering, product and customer operations. You will turn servicing workflows, such as making a payment, checking loan details, updating an address or enabling autopay, into production journeys and keep improving them after launch. You will build and own the journeys end to end, from first draft to steady state. The work is part builder, part analyst: design the flow, handle the edge cases, read the transcripts, and keep raising containment. Containment, CSAT, transfer quality and hallucination rate are your metrics.

 Within your first year, you will own a portfolio of journeys across products (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, HELOC, Deposits) and help set the standards for how Upgrade builds, tests and ships AI experiences.

 Our Core Technologies

 Sierra Agent Studio (no-code journeys), Sierra simulations and conversation analytics, GraphQL and REST APIs (as journey tools), Genesys (contact center handoff), SumoLogic, Grafana, SQL, Javascript/Typescript, Claude and other LLM tools.

 What You'll Do

 • Journey creation: Design and build Sierra journeys in Agent Studio for chat, voice and email, from discovery with operations through production rollout

 • Optimization: Review transcripts, recordings and analytics every week, find where conversations fail or transfer, and ship fixes to journey logic, instructions and knowledge

 • Edge case handling: Map the unhappy paths (failed payments, mismatched identity, delinquent accounts, unsupported requests) and make sure each ends in a correct answer or a clean handoff

 • Containment: Own containment and CSAT targets per journey, run staged rollouts (1% → 100%), and prioritize the work that moves those numbers most

 • Product partnership: Work with product groups (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, Deposits) to scope new journeys, keep journeys current as products change, and define the APIs the agent needs

 • Safety and compliance: Apply tiered authentication and step-up verification, verbatim compliance language and guardrails against hallucination and off-policy answers

 • Handoffs: Design transfers to human agents in Genesys with accurate summaries and auth context

 • Testing: Build simulation and regression suites so every journey change ships with evidence it did not break existing behavior

 • Monitoring: Watch latency, errors and drop-offs in SumoLogic and Grafana, and own the alerts

 • Voice tuning: Latency, filler phrases, interruptions, personality and tone

 • Sierra relationship: Be the technical owner on our side, escalate platform issues and shape roadmap asks

 What We Look For:

 • 3–5 years of Frontend Software Engineering experience, or equivalent experience in Solutions Engineering, Conversational AI or Technical Product roles

 • Working knowledge of how LLM agents behave: instructions, tool calls, knowledge retrieval, and where each one fails

 • Experience building evaluations for non-deterministic systems: test sets, simulations, LLM-as-judge, regression gates

 • Enough technical depth to read API specs, work with backend engineers on REST and GraphQL integrations, and reason about authorization and permission scopes

 • Working knowledge of JavaScript/TypeScript, with the ability to build and maintain coded journeys and integrate APIs within conversational AI platforms.

 • Product and customer mindset: you understand ops procedures, you read transcripts, care about tone, and measure success by whether the customer's problem got solved

 • Ownership in production: rollouts, monitoring, log analysis and incident response

 • Clear writing and the ability to work with non-engineers in operations, compliance and legal

 Nice To Have:

 • Hands-on experience with Sierra Agent Studio, or a comparable no-code agent platform (Decagon, Ada, Kore.ai, Google CCAI, Amazon Lex/Connect)

 • Voice AI experience: speech-to-text, text-to-speech, latency tuning, barge-in handling

 • Contact center systems such as Genesys, and agent handoff design

 • Background in fintech or another regulated industry (UDAAP, FDCPA, TCPA, PCI, SOC 2)

 • Conversation design or UX writing experience

 What We Offer You:

 • Competitive salary ($140K-$180K CAN) and stock option plan

 • Paid coverage of medical, dental and vision insurance

 • Flexible PTO

 • Opportunities for professional growth and development
• Paid parental leave

 • Health & wellness initiatives

 To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/upgrade-ai-experience-engineer-conversational-ai

title: Customer Solutions Engineer, EMEA
description:
Headquarters: Remote - Ireland

 About the Role

 Abnormal AI is looking for a Customer Solutions Engineer to join the Technical Account Management team. This role gives Abnormal a flexible, technical resource for situations that fall between standard support and a long-term, dedicated Technical Account Manager. Customer Solutions Engineers are floating technical specialists who partner with CSMs for the duration of a specific need, triggered by things like recurring support cases, asks beyond the typical support experience, or short-term project-based work. The ideal candidate combines deep technical fluency with strong triage judgment and is comfortable moving between engagements without an existing playbook.

 What you will do

• Serve as a flexible technical resource CSMs can bring into challenging or recurring account situations that a standard support case isn't built to resolve.

• Take on short-term, project-based technical engagements for customers without a dedicated TAM.

• Partner with CSMs to assess customer technical needs, join investigative or best-practices calls, and determine the right next step.

• Lead hands-on platform optimization: configuration reviews, best-practices setup, and proactive tuning that prevents issues from recurring.

• Document session recaps and next steps in the CRM so recommendations are clear to the customer and visible to the broader team.

• Advise customers on underused contracted features and flag upsell or professional services/deployment opportunities where relevant.

• Recognize when a situation exceeds this role's scope and hand it to the Critical Situation Manager or Technical Support with a clear, documented hand-off.

• Surface patterns across engagements to Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to drive systemic improvement.

 Must Haves

• 3+ years in a customer-facing technical role (email infrastructure, IT security/administration, engineering, or technical support) in enterprise SaaS or cybersecurity

• Solid grounding in Abnormal's platform and configuration best practices, sufficient to work independently with customers without a senior technical resource in the room

• Strong triage judgment; able to recognize quickly whether a situation calls for hands-on technical guidance or a more senior technical resource

• Comfortable stepping into a customer relationship for a defined engagement and stepping back out; this is not a standing account-ownership role

• Able to manage multiple concurrent, time-bound engagements across a broad book of business rather than a fixed set of named accounts

• Excellent communication skills across technical and business stakeholders, including comfort presenting to senior customer stakeholders

 Nice to Have

• Familiarity with email authentication/delivery protocols and cloud email platforms (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace)

• Prior experience in a floating/pooled technical resource model (e.g., professional services, deployment, or solutions engineering)

• Bachelor's degree in a technical field, or equivalent hands-on experience

 Abnormal AI uses AI-assisted tools to help our recruiting team prepare for candidate interviews. These tools analyze resume content and role requirements to suggest interview questions and areas for the interviewer to explore.They do not make hiring decisions or screen candidates automatically. title: Director, Delivery Solutions Architects - Public Sector
description:
Headquarters: Maryland; Remote - Virginia; Remote - Washington D.C.

 CSQ427R326

 Please note: Due to federal contract requirements and client-site access obligations, U.S. citizenship is required .

 As Director of Delivery Solution Architects (DSA), Public Sector, you will lead a high-impact post-sales technical organization that helps government customers realize value from the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. Your mission is to ensure that complex Data and AI initiatives—across federal civilian, defense, intelligence, state and local government, education, and public-sector-adjacent organizations—move from concept to production as quickly, securely, and effectively as possible.

 You will lead DSA managers and a growing team of Delivery Solution Architects responsible for technical strategy, customer outcomes, platform adoption, and usage growth across the Public Sector. You will bridge technical strategy and durable customer value, ensuring teams guide customers through architecture decisions, implementation planning, and scalable operating models for data, analytics, AI, and agentic applications.

 You will make investment and coverage decisions in collaboration with regional Sales and Field Engineering leaders, shape the value proposition of the DSA function for Public Sector, and build an organization that delivers predictable customer outcomes in a complex, high-growth environment.

 The Impact You Will Have:

• Build and lead: Recruit, coach, and scale a diverse, high-performing team of DSAs and managers. Foster a culture of psychological safety, collaboration, and customer obsession.

•
 Define, operationalize, and continuously improve the post-sales execution strategy for Databricks’ Public Sector business.

•
 Partner with Sales, Solutions Architecture, Professional Services, Customer Success, and strategic partners to align account plans, technical success plans, resource investments, and growth strategies.

•
 Establish scalable account assignments, customer coverage, prioritization, capacity planning, and resource-allocation practices for strategic Public Sector accounts.

•
 Standardize how DSAs guide customers from use-case discovery and architecture through implementation, production go-live, adoption, and platform expansion.

•
 Lead a technically excellent DSA organization with deep expertise in cloud data platforms, data engineering, warehousing, ETL/ELT, streaming, governance, machine learning, generative AI, and agentic applications.

•
 Ensure customers receive practical, secure, scalable architectural guidance for production data products, analytics platforms, AI applications, and mission-critical workloads.

•
 Apply Public Sector-specific requirements—including security, compliance, governance, mission continuity, procurement, and complex stakeholder environments—to architecture and delivery decisions.

•
 Serve as a trusted executive technical advisor for select strategic customers, linking technical roadmaps and modernization programs to agency missions and measurable outcomes.

•
 Build strong executive and operational relationships across customer technical, program, procurement, operational, and leadership stakeholders to accelerate adoption and long-term value.

•
 Create operating mechanisms, playbooks, metrics, and review cadences to monitor customer health, delivery progress, adoption, usage growth, risks, escalations, and forecasted expansion.

•
 Drive cross-functional resolution of delivery blockers and escalations, while providing leadership feedback on field processes, product needs, programs, and organizational investments.

 What We Look For:

• 7+ years of customer-facing experience in technical delivery, architecture, consulting, customer success, professional services, or post-sales leadership roles.

description:
Cover Supervisor

Rickmansworth School

About the role

Location: Croxley Green, Rickmansworth

Contract type: Term time plus 2 INSET/Additional Days, Permanent

Hours: 18 hours per week: Tuesday - Thursday, 08:20 - 15:20

This is a fantastic opportunity to make a real impact on students’ learning and development.
As a Cover Supervisor you will play a key role in maintaining continuity of learning during teacher absences. You will supervise whole classes, ensuring that students remain on task and complete work set by their usual teacher or department.

You will be an essential part of our school community, helping to create a calm, purposeful classroom environment. While you will not be required to plan or mark work, your ability to manage behaviour, support learning and uphold school policies will be vital in keeping students engaged and productive.

If you are confident, organised, and enthusiastic about working with young people, we would love to hear from you. Join us in supporting students to thrive and achieve their best every day.

In return, we will offer you:

  • Outstanding CPD opportunities to support your professional growth

  • A school with exemplary student behaviour, where learning is valued

  • A collaborative working environment where teamwork is at the heart of everything we do

  • A comprehensive wellbeing programme to ensure you feel valued and supported

Rickmansworth School is an outstanding, heavily over-subscribed 11-18 co-educational academy, consistently achieving excellent academic results. We provide a nurturing and dynamic environment for our 1575 ambitious young people. Our strong academic track record at both GCSE and A-Level ensures that the vast majority of our students go on to their first-choice universities.

Further information is available from our website - https://www.rickmansworth.herts.sch.uk

We encourage potential candidates to contact Rickmansworth School for an informal discussion about the role or to arrange a visit to the School if they have any specific questions, please contact the School on 01923 773296 or email applications@rickmansworth.herts.sch.uk.

We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and are an equal opportunities employer who has a zero tolerance to bullying and all types of harassment. Applicants must declare any criminal convictions and submit to a check with the Disclosing and Barring Service as the post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974.

Interviews: TBC

Selection Process:

We are required for only shortlisted candidates to conduct online searches about an applicant as part of our shortlisting process in accordance with Keeping Children Safe in Education guidance 2025 in order to identify any incidents or concerns which are publicly available online. Interviews will be held with the Headteacher and possibly another member of SLT. There will also be a tour of the school estate and this may be conducted by other members of the school community.

title: Whole School Admissions and Transitions Coordinator
description:
At Greenshaw High School, we know that excellent schools rely on dedicated staff in every role. We are looking for a committed Whole School Admissions and Transitions Coordinator to join our team and support the smooth running of the school.

About the Role

We are looking for an enthusiastic, highly motivated individual to join our committed School Office team as a maternity cover. The successful candidate will motivate, challenge, support and inspire our students. They must also have relevant experience in a similar role with a proven track record.

The post holder will be responsible for the day-to-day provision of all aspects of the admissions and transitions procedures in the school using the schools Management Information Systems, SAM (local authority system), Admissions+ and schools messaging software, whilst playing an integral part of the admin team to ensure that a professional and efficient administrative service is provided at all times. You will be expected to work during the GCSE results week in August each year to ensure the smooth enrolment of all 6th form students including the administration that accompanies this event. In addition to this you will be expected to attend the after school Open Evenings and other relevant events.

Key aspects of the role include:

  • To manage all student admissions to the school, including sixth form
  • To maintain the school Management Information System ensuring that information is recorded accurately and that the data is reviewed and updated regularly
  • Accurately record the number of students on roll and any criteria with regard to funding for the Headteacher and Director of Operations
  • Providing an efficient administrative service to the school to include but not exclusively; mail merges, producing labels and any other admin task that the school requests

We're Looking For Someone Who:

  • Has experience working within an admissions role
  • Has excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate with colleagues, students, parents and other visitors in a professional manner
  • Has practical experience of word processing, excel, e-mail and other office electronic applications
  • Ability to show initiative and work under pressure, multi-task and work to strict timelines

Why join Greenshaw High School and Greenshaw Learning Trust?

Greenshaw High School is a highly over-subscribed 11 to 18 mixed comprehensive secondary school situated in Sutton, South West London. We are proud of our strong local reputation, having over 4,000 applications for 300 places in September 2024. In October 2024 the hard work of our students and staff was recognised by Ofsted. The inspection team described the school as offering "an exceptional standard of education", using the words "flourishing, "inclusive" and "friendly" to describe our school. In the report Quality of Education, Behaviour & Attitudes, Sixth Form and Leadership & Management were all graded as Outstanding.

We have a very diverse population of students, offering a comprehensive range of opportunities for colleagues who work here. Our students - of all groups - have done incredibly well over the last few years, with our GCSE achievement always being at least in the top 20% of the country, and over 60 Sixth Form students attending Russell Group universities each year.

Greenshaw Learning Trust is a highly successful multi academy trust that provides excellent quality, comprehensive and inclusive education through primary schools and secondary schools. Our schools are based in London, Surrey, Berkshire, Gloucestershire and South Gloucestershire, Bristol and Plymouth. We also have three shared service hubs where our central teams can be based out of. We are building a family of like-minded schools, that collaborate to provide mutual support, share their good practice and learn from each other, whilst retaining and developing their own distinctive character. We thrive from collaboration at every level. We encourage a culture of sharing ideas and learning from one another. As a Trust of schools, we are ‘Always Learning’.

To get a feel of life at Greenshaw Learning Trust, please download our ‘Why you should work for GLT’ recruitment brochure on our jobs portal.

We offer our staff a range of benefits including:

  • Professional development and career progression
  • Generous pension scheme
  • Blue Light Card
  • An Employee Assistance Programme
  • Gym Discounts
  • Free eye tests
  • Car Benefit Scheme
  • Cycle to work scheme
  • Being part of a great team and expanding organisation

title: Teaching Assistant
description:
Our Trust

At the heart of our Catholic Multi-Academy Trust is a mission that shapes everything we do. Inspired by the witness of St Gabriel the Archangel, we are Forming Christ-centred pilgrims of hope with kind hearts, questioning minds, a thirst for knowledge, and a hunger for justice. These characteristics are lived out in our schools, they shape our culture, leadership, teaching, and our community. St Gabriel the Archangel Catholic Multi-Academy Trust is a family of 64 schools working together to provide high-quality, faith-filled education to every child we serve.

About this Role

St Mary’s Catholic Primary School, Brewood, is a welcoming and inclusive school with a warm, supportive atmosphere, open to families of all faiths. We are committed to high standards in wellbeing, behaviour, and personal development, alongside a strong community ethos and enriching opportunities for every child. As part of St Gabriel the Archangel Catholic Multi-Academy Trust, we provide a nurturing environment where children—and staff—can thrive.

We are looking for a dedicated and compassionate Teaching Assistant to join our team.

The successful candidate will provide support to pupils, helping them engage with the curriculum, develop their skills and build confidence in a positive, nurturing and inclusive environment.

We are looking for someone who is patient, caring and enthusiastic, with a genuine commitment to supporting children and helping them achieve their full potential.

Required to start as soon as possible!

32.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday, term-time only plus INSETS

Full-time but a job share may be considered

About the Role:

We are looking for someone:

To provide support to pupils across the classroom, helping them to engage positively with their learning and develop their skills and confidence.

To demonstrate a patient, caring and proactive approach when supporting pupils with a range of abilities and learning needs.

To foster a positive, inclusive and engaging learning environment that encourages pupils to participate, develop their independence and achieve their potential.

To support the teacher with classroom activities, assisting pupils with tasks and adapting resources and approaches where appropriate to meet individual learning needs.

To work collaboratively with the class teacher and wider school team to support pupils’ learning, progress and personal development.

To encourage positive behaviour, social skills, confidence and independence, helping pupils to develop effective learning habits.

To monitor and support pupils’ progress, providing feedback to the class teacher and contributing to observations and records where appropriate.

To assist with the preparation and organisation of classroom resources and learning activities.

title: Chef De Partie
description:
Work alongside and be mentored by the Head Chef at Christ’s College Finchley, Great British Menu Champion of Champions series 20, 2025- Amber Francis

Are you passionate about providing high quality nutrition for children and playing a key role in educating the next generation

on how they can develop and sustain a high-quality diet? This exceptional school seeks a highly talented individual for this post.

We have transformed the food provision for our pupils and expect the very highest standards to inspire young minds to make

the right choices for their health now and in the future. This is a unique opportunity for an inspirational Chef De Partie.

At Christ’s College Finchley, we have a long history of success. We strive to advance all the way by combining the most enduring

aspects of the CCF traditions (including high academic standards, excellent behaviour and a commitment to the personal and

social development of our pupils) with effective, innovative approaches to teaching and learning. The successful candidate will

be committed to our vision of high standards of nutrition and food education for all children.

ADVANCE YOUR CAREER

At Christ’s College Finchley we value our staff by providing a positive school climate. Our aim is to ensure a balanced,

secure and healthy workplace where our teaching and support staff can flourish. We do this because we know that our staff

are central to the success of our pupils.

Your passion for education will be evident along with essential qualities such as the ability to communicate effectively, the

ability to listen and the ability to collaborate and work with others. You will have that unique skill of monitoring and

inspiring our young people and in return we will provide you with every opportunity for a rewarding career.

Christ’s College Finchley has a high-performing workforce and staff talent which is evident by the low levels of staff

absences and turnover. Our staff wellbeing approach is a priority and, along with our focus on promoting from within, is

central to our staff retention strategy. We place great emphasis on reviewing individual workloads and time pressures to

ensure there are flexible work routines; workplace support and integration; individual and team recognition; and positive

working relationships to maintain and improve the mental and physical wellbeing of our staff.

In the same way that we have high expectations of our pupils, we have high expectations of our staff but the benefits and

CAREER, HEALTH AND WEALTH BENEFITS

believe that staff can only discharge their responsibility for pupils if their own wellbeing is strong and therefore we prioritise

  • Free tea and coffee in our large staff room.

  • A range of social events including summer barbeques and winter socials. Cake at Break takes place every Wednesday.

  • On-site free parking.

  • A scheduled calendar for staff, published in advance, with flexibility for events such as parents' evenings, which take place

    virtually, and a commitment to remaining under directed time.

  • Trained Mental Health First Aiders.

  • Eligible staff are entitled to an eye test and a contribution towards corrective glasses where they are required specifically

    for display screen equipment use.

  • Membership of the Schools Advisory Service which provides access for staff to a range of benefits including: GP

    appointment, counselling, some operations, physiotherapy and menopause support.

title: Finance Officer
description:
Finance Officer

Location: Hayes, to work flexibly across all schools within the trust.

Salary: £31,288 to £32,655 per annum (Scale 4, Point 7-10 , dependant on experience)

Contract Type: Full-time permanent

Working Weeks: All year round

Hours: 36 hours per week - Monday to Friday, working between the hours of 8am and 4pm with an unpaid 40-minute lunch break

Reporting to: Trust Financial Controller

About Us: Our multi-academy trust is dedicated to providing exceptional educational opportunities for young people, fostering inclusive learning environments, and nurturing a strong sense of community. With three schools under our care—Barnhill High School, Belmore Primary, and William Byrd Primary—our mission is to ensure every child has access to outstanding facilities that inspire success.

What We Offer:

  • The opportunity to make a significant impact across multiple schools.
  • A supportive and collaborative working environment.
  • Professional development opportunities to help you grow and succeed in your role.
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.

About the Role

We are seeking a proactive, organised, and highly motivated Finance Officer to join our Trust Finance Team.

The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the effective financial management of the Trust, ensuring that financial transactions are processed accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with Trust policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements. Working collaboratively with colleagues across all schools and central services, the postholder will help deliver a professional, high-quality finance service that supports educational excellence.

This is a Trust-wide role. The successful candidate will be expected to work flexibly across all schools within the Trust as required and contribute positively to a culture of teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

The postholder will build effective working relationships with school leaders, budget holders, administrative staff, suppliers, and Trust colleagues, providing a professional and customer-focused finance service. They will be an active member of the Trust Finance Team, supporting colleagues, sharing knowledge, and contributing to the continuous improvement of financial processes and controls across the Trust.

Key Responsibilities

Review and process purchase orders through Sage Intacct, ensuring orders are appropriately authorised, issued to suppliers promptly, and matched accurately to goods received and supplier invoices. Post invoices to the correct ledger codes and cost centres.

Prepare the fortnightly BACS payment run, ensuring all payments are accurately processed and appropriately authorised in accordance with the Trust's Scheme of Delegation and financial procedures

Administer school charge cards, ensuring expenditure is appropriately authorised, supported by documentation, accurately recorded, and reviewed against monthly statements.

Administer 16-19 Bursary payments and support schools with associated bursary administration and financial processes.

Administer the Trust's cashless payment platform, including the setup of payment offers, monitoring income received, reporting on outstanding balances, and supporting the collection of overdue payments.

Raise sales invoices and monitor outstanding debtors, undertaking credit control activities and escalating concerns where necessary.

Process, reconcile, and bank income received across the Trust, ensuring funds are handled securely, recorded accurately, and accounted for in accordance with Trust financial procedures

Respond professionally and efficiently to finance-related queries from staff, suppliers, and other stakeholders, ensuring issues are resolved in a timely manner.

Maintain accurate financial records across the Trust, including debtors, creditors, prepayments, accruals, journals, inter-school recharges, and monthly balance sheet reconciliations.

Prepare and reconcile monthly VAT reports to support the Trust's VAT reclaim process and ensure compliance with HMRC requirements.

Assist with the annual external audit by providing accurate information and supporting documentation in a timely manner.

Ensure all financial records and supporting documentation are maintained in an organised, secure, and auditable manner in line with Trust retention and archiving requirements.

Ensure all financial transactions and processes are carried out in accordance with the Trust's Finance Policy, Scheme of Delegation, Academy Trust Handbook, and all other relevant statutory, regulatory, and Trust requirements.

Ensure compliance with the Trust's financial regulations, policies, procedures, and internal controls, promoting strong financial governance and best practice across the Trust.

Undertake any other duties commensurate with the grade and responsibilities of the post as may reasonably be required by the Financial Controller, Chief Finance Officer, or other senior leaders.

Person Specification

AAT level 3 or working towards the qualification is desirable

Experience of working within a finance, accounting, or financial administration environment. Knowledge of Sage Intacct is desirable.

Strong numerical and analytical skills with excellent attention to detail.

Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, and experience of using financial systems.

Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workloads and meet deadlines.

Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

Ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team.

Flexible and adaptable, with the willingness to work across all schools within the Trust as required.

Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels.

Commitment to maintaining confidentiality and handling sensitive information appropriately.

Further Information


Middlesex Learning Partnership is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.

Successful candidates will be subject to an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check.

It is an offence to apply for the position if you are barred from engaging regulated activity relevant to children.

Early applications are positively encouraged and the school reserves the right to shortlist and interview earlier than advertised.

We do not accept CV's.

We accept only employment and academic references; character references and those sent from generic email addresses (e.g., Gmail or Hotmail) will not be accepted.

Please see link to the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy

Please note that we hold the right to carry out online checks on applicants selected for interview.

Middlesex Learning Partnership is a disability confident committed employer,

Closing Date: 29th October 2026.

title: Lead Product Manager
description:
Headquarters: Remote - Canada

 What You Will Do

 We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to own the future of the Lattice MCP (Model Context Protocol) server and the integrations that power Lattice AI. This is the connective layer that lets customers use Lattice performance data inside the AI tools they already work in (Claude, ChatGPT, Glean, Microsoft Copilot, and Slack), and that brings third-party productivity data (e.g., Jira, GitHub, Linear, Zoom, Asana) into Lattice. As AI becomes the center of gravity for how companies work, this surface is how Lattice stays connected, interoperable, and indispensable. You’ll join a fully staffed engineering team ready to execute, and together you’ll make ecosystem interoperability a reason customers choose and stay with Lattice.

 If you enjoy solving complex problems, shaping platform strategy, and working with great internal and external partners, you’ll love the impact you can have here. As a Lead Product Manager for MCP & AI Ecosystem, you will:

• Own the MCP and AI ecosystem strategy. Not only decide what features and integrations to pursue, but what MCP and AI mean to Lattice and our customers. Become a thought leader on how AI should shape HR for the better.

• Ship integrations that create leverage. Deliver new MCP tools, resources, and third-party connectors that expand what admins, managers, and executives can do with Lattice data in the flow of work.

• Build durable foundations, like authentication, agentic execution frameworks, and evals that make future integrations faster, more scalable, and easier to adopt and maintain.

• Be a technical thought partner to Engineering. Help shape technical direction on MCP tool design and third party integration infrastructure, translating complex constraints into clear product decisions.

• Drive go-to-market with partners. Partner with Partnerships, Product Marketing, to launch integrations that deliver measurable customer and ecosystem impact.

• Own outcomes. Influence and own key results across integration and MCP adoption, reliability, activation, and ecosystem growth.

 What You Will Bring to the Table

 We’re looking for a seasoned product manager with the technical depth and strategic instincts to shape Lattice’s next generation of integrations and APIs. You’ll be a great fit if you have a combination of:

• 6+ years of product management experience, with meaningful ownership of integrations, platform, or ecosystem surfaces (built end-to-end, not just configured).

• Direct experience building technical integrations in a multi-party ecosystem — for example ad technology / marketing technology, marketplaces, developer platforms, payments, data connectivity, or similar — where partnership strategy shaped what you built.

• Strong technical fluency: comfortable with third-party integration patterns, data sync and field mapping, webhooks, and auth/OAuth; you can hold a credible architecture conversation with engineers and partner CTOs.

• A track record of shipping scalable, reliable integrations in partnership with engineering, and of standing up partner or marketplace launches with go-to-market teams.

• Evidence of turning a platform or ecosystem into a competitive advantage — a reason customers chose your product, not just a checkbox.

• Clear, confident communication that brings internal teams and external partners into alignment.

• A bias for action and the ability to create structure in an ambiguous, fast-moving space.

 Bonus:

• Exposure to AI ecosystems, MCP, AI agents, or LLM tooling (helpful, not required).

• Experience in multi-product B2B SaaS, or with HR/people-data or other sensitive-data workflows.

 If you have strong experience with integrations, APIs, or platform products, even if you don’t meet every preferred qualification, we encourage you to apply. We’re looking for strong product thinkers with deep technical fluency, not perfect resumes.

title: Senior Manager, Quality, Volume Tiers
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: https://careers.airbnb.com/life-at-airbnb/

 Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

 The Community You Will Join:

 The Senior Quality Lead, Volume Tiers is the single accountable leader for quality measurement, insights, and continuous improvement across Airbnb's highest-volume Community Support functions. This role owns the end-to-end quality program for:

• Global English (GE)

• Rest of World (ROW; which is comprised of 9 different languages)

• Elevated Support

 GE and ROW span across multiple service tiers: Resolutions 1, 2, and 3, Dedicated Service Support (DSS), Dedicated Managed Host Support (DMHS); supported across a global partner network operating 24/7 in dozens of languages.

 The Difference You will Make:

 This is a senior leadership role operating at the intersection of strategy and execution. The Senior Quality Lead will break down silos within the Quality organization, establish a unified operating model, and leverage AI-powered tools to scale quality insights. This leader will work closely with Service Delivery, Training, Business Process Improvement, and other stakeholders to ensure alignment on priorities, remediate issues, and ensure Airbnb is providing its global partner network a unified set of priorities.

 The successful candidate will establish themselves as a credible partner to stakeholders and be recognized internally as the voice of quality for the Volume Tier portfolio.

 A Typical Day:

 Strategic Leadership & Program Ownership

• Own and execute the Volume Tier quality strategy aligned to several critical priorities: breaking silos, aligning with stakeholders, defining a clear operating model, and driving measurable impact.

• Consolidate fragmented QA frameworks across GE and ROW into a unified operating model, eliminating inconsistent processes, divergent NPS detractor approaches, and incompatible quality signals.

• Represent Volume Tier quality in WBRs, MBRs, QBRs, and cross-functional planning forums; bring a proactive, narrative-led perspective that gives leadership visibility before problems surface in operational reviews.

 Measurement & Quality Execution

• Oversee QA evaluation execution across all Volume Tier partner sites globally, ensuring consistent application of QA processes and frameworks.

• Lead root cause analysis on systemic failures, translating QA findings into product, process, and policy recommendations that go beyond agent-level coaching.

• Formalize Audit the Auditor as an ongoing control: define sample selection, alignment thresholds, root cause review, and evaluator-level remediation processes.

• Ensure every evaluation closes with a documented coaching action; build the tracking mechanisms to measure whether coaching is translating into performance improvement over time.

 Insights, Reporting & Stakeholder Partnership

• Establish automated KPI reporting across all Volume Tier sites, tiers, and languages, eliminating manual processes.

• Unify NPS detractor analysis across GE and ROW, ensuring global patterns surface in real time.

• Build a Partner QA Performance Scorecard, establishing clear accountability for Calibration Accuracy, Evaluation Completeness, Critical Error Detection, Coaching Effectiveness.

 AI & Technology Enablement

• Lead the deployment of AutoQA (via Observe.AI) across Volume Tiers; partner with the Platform team to ensure appropriate sequencing.

• Build and govern a clear accountability framework for AI-assisted quality tools and processes.

 People & Culture Leadership

• Lead a globally distributed team of Partner Quality Leads and Quality Insights Analysts.

• Foster a One-Quality-Team culture that eliminates the cross-team divides: shared best practices, cross-regional learning, and proactive knowledge sharing.

• Set high expectations and hold the team accountable for output quality, insight delivery, and stakeholder engagement.

• Partner closely with peers to ensure one consistent quality voice across the portfolio.

 Your Expertise:

• 12+ years of experience in Customer/Community Support, Quality Assurance, or Contact Center Operations, with direct accountability for large-scale, multilingual QA programs.

• 5+ years managing globally distributed QA teams across multiple languages, regions, and partner organizations in a 24/7 support environment.

• Bachelor's Degree or equivalent experience, preferably in related field; MBA or Masters preferred

• Experience with QA tooling platforms, including hands-on ownership of form design, calibration management, and AutoQA deployment.

• Deep expertise in quality methodologies (COPC, AQS, Six Sigma, Lean), with a proven ability to apply them to high-volume, complex support environments.

• Demonstrated track record of leading quality transformation, consolidating fragmented programs, driving measurable improvement in NPS/CSAT, and QA calibrations.

• Experience deploying or scaling AI/ML assisted QA tools (AutoQA, predictive NPS/CSAT).

• Strong executive presence: able to influence senior stakeholders, present a unified quality narrative in leadership forums, and drive alignment across stakeholders.

• Experience managing vendor partner governance: calibration oversight, performance improvement plans, and escalation frameworks.

 Preferred

• COPC certification; Six Sigma Green or Black Belt.

• Experience with Observe.AI.

• Background in program management, change management, or organizational design within a high-growth tech environment.

• Experience working in or closely with BPO/vendor governance models at scale (1,000+ partner FTEs across multiple sites and geographies).

 Your Location:

 This position is Canada - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a province where Airbnb Canada, Inc. has a registered entity. Currently we can hire in the following provinces: Ontario, British Columbia, Quebec, Alberta, and Saskatchewan. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with your recruiter on what provinces you are eligible to work from.

 Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging:

 Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

 We strive to also provide a disability inclusive application and interview process. If you are a candidate with a disability and require reasonable accommodation in order to submit an application, please contact us at: reasonableaccommodations@airbnb.com. Please include your full name, the role you’re applying for and the accommodation necessary to assist you with the recruiting process.

 We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application.

 We use automated tools to help our recruiting team efficiently screen a large volume of applications. All final hiring decisions are made by a human reviewer.

 This role is newly created and does not replace or backfill an existing position.

 How We'll Take Care of You:

 Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands. The base pay range shown below is annualized, is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role may also be eligible for bonus, equity, benefits, and Employee Travel Credits.

 Canada Annual Pay Range

 $160,000—$200,000 CAD

 Reasonable Accommodations: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.

 A Note on Recruiting Scams: Scammers sometimes pose as Airbnb recruiters to get money or personal information from candidates. A few things that will always be true for Airbnb’s hiring process: our open roles are posted on Airbnb’s Career’s Page at careers.airbnb.com, and our recruiters correspond only from @airbnb.com or @ext.airbnb.com email addresses. Our recruiters will never ask for your Social Security number, bank account details, passport, or payment app information while you are interviewing. We’ll also never ask you to pay a fee, send money, deposit or cash a check, or purchase work-related equipment (such as a company laptop) during the interview process. We encourage candidates to remain vigilant of these recruiting scams and not share sensitive information if you do not believe an individual is actually affiliated with Airbnb.

title: VP, Finance
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: https://engine.com/

 About the Role

 We're looking for a VP, Finance to lead Finance at Engine and serve as a strategic partner to our CEO and executive leadership team.

 You'll own the financial strategy and operating cadence of the company, from planning and forecasting to capital allocation, business performance, financial reporting, and long-range strategy. You'll help leadership understand what is driving the business, where we should invest, and what we need to do next. You'll also be the architect of Engine's financial story, shaping how the company is understood by its Board, investors, and partners.

 You'll build the Finance organization and infrastructure to support Engine through its next phase of growth. That means creating clarity where there is ambiguity, building scalable processes before they become bottlenecks, and using data, systems, and AI to make Finance increasingly leveraged.

 Success in this role will be measured by business impact and the results of the Finance organization.

 What You'll Do

 Strategic Financial Leadership

• Serve as the CEO's financial thought partner on growth strategy, investment priorities, resource allocation, and profitability. Drive capital allocation decisions across the executive team — where Engine invests people, capital, and resources, and where we make tradeoffs. Bring financial rigor to pricing, monetization, new products, markets, and partnerships.

 Capital Strategy & Transactions

• Own fundraising, debt and liquidity strategy, M&A, and other strategic transactions. Build investor relationships, lead the Board story on performance, and prepare Engine for future capital events — including the reporting, controls, and governance a public-ready company requires (SOX readiness, audit committee partnership, external guidance frameworks).

 Financial Planning & Business Insight

• Own the financial plan — quarterly forecasting, long-range modeling, scenario analysis, and the operating cadence across Engine. Develop a deep understanding of revenue, margins, customer economics, pricing, payment economics, and cash flow. Build the metrics and frameworks that make the business legible to leadership.

 Narrative & Communication

• Tell Engine's financial story to the Board, investors, lenders, and partners — turning complex numbers into a narrative leadership can act on and external audiences believe. Lead financial reporting and help the CEO communicate performance, outlook, risks, opportunities, and key decisions with clarity.

 Build Finance for Scale

• Build and lead a high-performance Finance team — attracting exceptional talent, modernizing through AI and automation, and establishing systems, processes, data infrastructure, and controls that scale without creating bureaucracy. Partner with Accounting, Treasury, Legal, and external advisors to ensure Engine has the financial foundation required to scale responsibly.

 What You'll Bring

 Experience and Background

• 12+ years of experience across investment banking, private equity, growth equity, corporate finance, FP&A, strategic finance, or a related field, with significant experience in high-growth technology.

• Investment banking or private equity background, with hands-on experience in valuation, transaction execution, and capital markets. Strongly preferred.

• Experience leading Finance, or a major component of Finance, at a high-growth tech, SaaS, marketplace, fintech, or similarly complex company.

 Financial Expertise

• Exceptional financial modeling skills and a strong understanding of three-statement modeling, unit economics, cash flow, and capital allocation.

• A track record of building financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and analytical infrastructure in environments that are scaling quickly.

• Experience evaluating pricing, monetization, new products, investments, headcount, and other strategic decisions.

 Communication and Partnership

• A track record of communicating complex financial stories to investors, boards, and executive teams in ways that drive decisions and build confidence.

• Experience partnering directly with a CEO, executive team, and Board.

 Leadership and Team Building

• Experience building and developing high-performing Finance teams. Comfort operating without a fully defined playbook and building structure where it doesn’t exist.

 Judgment and Execution

• Strong commercial instincts. You understand that Finance exists to help the business make better decisions, not simply to explain what happened last quarter.

• The ability to operate at both the strategic and tactical level and an usually high bar for execution and bias towards action

• Strong conviction and judgment. You bring a point of view vs just presenting options.

 Compensation
Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, all roles receive equity. Depending on the role, total compensation may also include an annual bonus. Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

 Base Pay Range

 $300,000 - $375,000 USD

 The Engine Edge: Perks & Compensation
We believe in rewarding great work with great benefits:

• Compensation: Competitive base pay tied to role and experience, with equity for all employees. Some roles are also eligible for bonuses or commissions.

• Benefits: Check out our full list at engine.com/culture

• Environments for Success: Different roles have different needs in terms of the environments that drive success which is why we have a hybrid-hub model. Whether you are in one of our amazing offices or fully remote, we'll make sure you have what you need to succeed.

 Perks and benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and more

title: Sales Development Representative - Service Provider
description:
Headquarters: Remote US

 What We Do:

 Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations. That pushes defenders like us to operate at the highest level, and it deepens our need for good people who want to make a meaningful impact.

 Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress is a remote-first team working to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to businesses of all sizes. We work closely with security teams and service providers protecting complex environments, often without the time or headcount to handle it all. That’s why we build our technology in-house and back it with a 24/7 human-led Security Operations Center (SOC). As a result, our platform is never disconnected from the experts who manage it, ensuring our customers' protection.

 Huntress now secures more than 5M endpoints and 16M identities worldwide. Those numbers keep growing because more businesses rely on us to help carry the load and operate with more confidence. Every day, you can see that commitment in how we stand with our customers and how we show up for each other.

 Reports to: SDR Manager

 Location: Remote US

 Compensation Range: $58,500 base with on target earnings at $78,000 plus equity

 What You'll Do:

 Huntress is looking for a talented and passionate Sales Development Representative (SDR) to help fuel our continued growth. In this role, you will open doors for the Account Executive team by building relationships with managed service providers (MSPs) and managed security service providers (MSSPs), earning trust quickly, and turning early conversations into qualified meetings that move the pipeline forward. You are outcome-obsessed in how you work, with a clear eye on the right next step, the right partner fit, and the follow-through it takes to create real pipeline impact.

 In the daily rhythm of prospecting into the MSP and MSSP space, you bring warrior spirit. You stay steady through rejection, keep your standards high, and come back sharper on the next call. You also give a sh*t about the people on the other end of the phone, leading with honesty, curiosity, and respect as you help prospective partners understand the value Huntress can deliver to their business and their customers.

 Responsibilities:

• Establish rapport and trust with managed service provider (MSP) and managed security service provider (MSSP) prospects via phone, email, and LinkedIn to understand their business and their fit with Huntress.

• Set qualified meetings within our ideal customer profile by following best practices and standard processes.

• Generate and qualify net-new accounts and work inbound opportunities to create a pipeline for the Account Executive team.

• Use clear, value-driven messaging to build interest in Huntress and answer prospect questions with honesty, professionalism, and empathy.

• Research accounts, document prospecting activity, and qualification notes in CRM, and maintain strong data hygiene.

• Use AI tools with good judgment to support account research, call prep, and message drafting in your day-to-day work.

• Keep improving your cold calling, messaging, and pipeline management skills through training, feedback, and repetition.

 What You Bring to the Team:

• 8+ months of experience in a quota-carrying outbound B2B SaaS sales role.

• Experience with outbound cold calling.

• Strong time management and the ability to prioritize competing tasks.

• Comfort working across CRM, prospecting tools, and multiple systems at the same time.

• Attention to detail when taking notes, setting meetings, and following the process.

• A coachable mindset and a genuine interest in continuing to grow your sales and cybersecurity knowledge.

• Curiosity about AI and the judgment to use it in practical ways that help you work faster and smarter in your day-to-day.

 What We Offer:

• 100% remote work environment - since our founding in 2015

• Generous paid time off policy, including vacation, sick time, and paid holidays

• 12 weeks of paid parental leave

• Highly competitive and comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits plans

• 401(k) with a 5% contribution regardless of employee contribution

description:
Headquarters: Remote - Mexico

 Who we are

 At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

 Our dedication to remote-first work , and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.
 .

 Hiring and how we work

 We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!

 Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.
 .

 See yourself at Twilio

 Join the team as Twilio’s next Billing Operations Analyst.

 Twilio is looking for a talented and results driven person who is passionate about work, savvy about billing and pricing from the business view not only financial and who lives the Twilio Magic They also have:

 Outstanding communication skills, both written and verbal, and ability to advocate for a position while maintaining a collaborative, and open-minded approach. You should be someone who is a champion of streamlining processes and sees projects through to completion. We are looking for someone who enjoys and thrives in a fast-paced environment, with zealous attention to detail, good judgment, and is dedicated to providing excellent customer service.

 Responsibilities

 In this role you’ll:
